# Design: Anthropic, OpenRouter and other LLM APIs behind one agent loop

Written 2026-10-19 on `jusprin-newui`. Working document, untracked.

## Summary

JusPrin's in-app agent talks to exactly one API today: OpenAI's Responses API, through `OpenAIResponsesAgent` (613 lines). That class does three jobs at once: it runs the tool-call turn loop, it builds and parses the Responses wire format, and it holds OpenAI-specific choices such as which tools get `strict: true`. Setup, configuration and three test harnesses are hard-wired to that class and to that wire format.

The proposal is to split the class into a provider-neutral turn loop plus one small "codec" per API family, and to describe each provider as data (endpoint, auth header, default model, error wording). After the split, OpenRouter costs one data entry because it serves an OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint. Anthropic costs one codec file of roughly 350 lines plus a schema projection. Any later OpenAI-compatible host (Groq, Together, Ollama, a local proxy) costs a data entry, or a third codec if it only speaks Chat Completions.

The MCP server needs no change. It shares only the tool registry with the LLM side, and the registry stays the single definition of every tool. One shared constraint did turn up: the registry's schemas use keywords that Anthropic's strict mode rejects, and the fix belongs in the Anthropic codec, not the registry.

## What exists today

| Piece | File | Provider-neutral? |
|---|---|---|
| `IAgentService`: start a turn, continue after a tool result, poll typed events | `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentService.hpp` | Yes |
| `AgentRequest`, `AgentConversationContext`: instructions, workspace, attachments, skills, earlier calls with their results | same | Yes |
| `IAgentHttpTransport`: one streaming POST, events queued to the GUI thread | `OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp`, `OpenAIHttpTransport.cpp` | Yes, except the request carries a single `authorization` string |
| Turn loop: queue a response's calls, run one at a time, answer later ones unrun after a failure, refuse unknown or invalid calls (two per turn), send images after results, send fired skills once, report usage, cancellation generations | `OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` | Yes in substance, but written against Responses JSON |
| Wire format: `instructions`, `input[]` items, `function_call` / `function_call_output`, SSE `response.*` events, `store:false`, `strict` per tool | `OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp` | No |
| Within-turn history: the raw `output[]` of each response, re-sent on every continuation | `m_input_history` | No. Carries OpenAI reasoning items, which must be echoed verbatim |
| Across-turn history: text plus call/result pairs, rebuilt by the host from the project document | `AgentHost.cpp` around line 2480 | Yes |
| Setup probe: one real request through the adapter | `AgentSetup.cpp` | Hard-codes `OpenAIResponsesAgent` |
| Runtime wiring and the `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` override | `AgentConfiguration.cpp` | Hard-codes `openai` |
| Setup page provider list | `AgentUI/src/components/Setup.tsx` | Lists Anthropic and Other as unavailable |
| Tool registry and MCP projection | `ToolRegistry.cpp`, `Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp` | Yes |

Three test surfaces read the Responses wire format directly: the 33 adapter tests in `tests/agent/test_openai_responses_agent.cpp`, the shell harness modes that record or hold request bodies (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, `project_prompt_scenario.inc`), and the Python prompt evals (`tests/project_prompt`, `tests/printer_prompt`), which replay recorded bodies against OpenRouter's Responses endpoint.

## Facts that decide the shape

Verified against current documentation on 2026-10-19:

- **OpenRouter serves a Responses API** at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses`. It is stateless and rejects `store: true` and `previous_response_id`. The adapter already sends `store: false` and replays the full turn, so the current request bodies are already in the shape OpenRouter wants. Tool calls use the same `function_call` / `function_call_output` items. The reasoning page is labelled beta. ([overview](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/responses/overview), [tool calling](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/responses/tool-calling))
- **Anthropic's OpenAI-compatible endpoint is not a shortcut.** Anthropic's own page says it ignores `strict`, drops prompt caching, merges every system message into one, and is meant for testing, not production. ([OpenAI SDK compatibility](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/openai-sdk)) Anthropic needs its native Messages API.
- **Anthropic strict mode rejects schema keywords the registry uses.** Unsupported: `minimum`, `maximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, and array constraints other than `minItems` of 0 or 1. The registry's schemas contain `maxItems` 55 times, `minimum` 13, `maxLength` 13, `maximum` 5, and one `minItems: 2`. A strict request with any of them is a 400. ([structured outputs limitations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs)) OpenAI accepts these keywords today; the live harness runs prove it.
- **Within one turn, both APIs need the assistant's output echoed verbatim.** OpenAI returns reasoning items with `encrypted_content` under `store: false` and asks for them back with the function outputs. ([reasoning guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning)) Anthropic wants the full `content[]` of the assistant message, thinking blocks included, and on Claude Opus 5.5 and later a changed earlier turn invalidates thinking blocks. The within-turn history therefore has to stay provider-shaped and opaque to the loop.
- **Across turns, both APIs accept a neutral record.** Text messages plus call/result pairs render as `function_call` + `function_call_output` on Responses and as an assistant `tool_use` block followed by a user `tool_result` block on Anthropic. The host already persists exactly this neutral record.
- **The current Claude models reject things the adapter never uses.** Forced `tool_choice`, assistant prefill, and `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` all return 400 on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5. The adapter uses none of them, so the Anthropic codec simply omits `thinking` and `tool_choice`.

## Proposed structure

```
IAgentService                      (unchanged)
  ProviderAgent                    the turn loop; today's OpenAIResponsesAgent minus the wire format
    IProviderCodec                 one per API family, pure JSON in and out, no network, no GUI
      ResponsesCodec               OpenAI, OpenRouter, any Responses-compatible host
      AnthropicCodec               Messages API
      ChatCompletionsCodec         later, only if a Chat-Completions-only host is wanted
    ProviderProfile                data: family, endpoint, auth style, default model, extra headers, error wording
    IAgentHttpTransport            unchanged, except headers become a list instead of one authorization string
```

### The loop and the transcript it owns

`ProviderAgent` keeps every rule the current class enforces, unchanged: one call runs at a time in the order written; a failed call answers the rest unrun; an unknown or invalid call is refused back to the model at most twice per turn; a result's image follows the results; fired skills ride on one request only; usage goes to the listener; a late event from a cancelled request is dropped by generation. All of that is expressed over a neutral transcript:

```
TurnTranscript
  instructions                      the session's text, byte-identical across the chat
  tools                             the ToolDefinitions offered this turn, plus skill_read's list
  opening                           earlier conversation (neutral records) + this turn's user content
  steps[]                           one per response so far:
    assistant_turn   json           opaque: output[] for Responses, content[] for Anthropic
    results[]                       call_id, state, output_json, optional image
    once[]                          skills fired by those results, sent on the next request only
```

The loop never looks inside `assistant_turn`. It gets the calls, the text deltas, the usage and the stop state from the codec's parsed events, and hands the opaque turn back to the same codec on the next request. A turn never changes provider, so the opaque value is always read by the codec that wrote it.

### The codec interface

Two functions, both deterministic and testable without a transport:

- `build(const TurnTranscript&, const ProviderProfile&, RequestKind) -> {body json, headers}`. `RequestKind` is the normal reply or the conversation-title request.
- `parse(const std::string& sse_data_payload) -> std::vector<StreamEvent>`. The loop keeps the SSE framing (it is identical across all three families) and passes each `data:` payload in. Events are neutral: `TextDelta`, `TurnComplete{assistant_turn, calls[], usage, stop}`, `Incomplete`, `Failed{code, retryable}`.

Anthropic's stream needs per-index accumulation of `input_json_delta` fragments before a call exists, so a codec is an object with a small amount of per-response state, reset by the loop at each request.

### Where each difference lives

| Concern | ResponsesCodec (OpenAI, OpenRouter) | AnthropicCodec | ChatCompletionsCodec (later) |
|---|---|---|---|
| System prompt | `instructions` | top-level `system` with a `cache_control` breakpoint | first message, role system |
| App notes mid-conversation (today's developer role) | role `developer` | role `system` inside `messages` (Opus 5, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable; no beta header); for older models, a user text in the app's tag | role `system` on OpenAI; a tagged user text elsewhere, since hosts differ |
| Tool definition | `{type:function, name, parameters, strict}` | `{name, description, input_schema, strict}`, `cache_control` on the last tool | `{type:function, function:{...}}` |
| Strict | registry schema as is, `strict` when the object tree is closed (today's rule) | project the schema: move `minimum`, `maximum`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `maxItems` and `minItems` above 1 into the property description, then `strict: true` | off by default; hosts vary |
| Tool result | `function_call_output` with a string `output` | `tool_result` with text and image blocks in one user message, all results of a response together | role `tool` messages, one per call |
| Image beside a result | separate user message after the results | image block inside the `tool_result` | separate user message |
| PDF attachment | `input_file` | `document` block, base64 | OpenRouter `file` part; otherwise text only |
| Streaming text | `response.output_text.delta` | `content_block_delta` with `text_delta` | `choices[0].delta.content` |
| Streaming calls | complete items in `response.completed` | `content_block_start` type `tool_use`, then `input_json_delta` fragments by index | `delta.tool_calls[i]` fragments by index |
| Terminal | `response.completed`, `incomplete`, `failed` | `message_delta` carries `stop_reason` and output usage; `message_stop` ends | `finish_reason` |
| Stop states | completed, incomplete | `end_turn`, `tool_use`, `max_tokens` (Incomplete), `refusal` (Failed, not retryable, with the category), `pause_turn` (resend) | `stop`, `tool_calls`, `length` |
| Usage | `input_tokens`, `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` | `input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `output_tokens` | `prompt_tokens`, `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, with `stream_options.include_usage` |
| Prompt cache | automatic on a stable prefix | explicit: breakpoint on the last tool, the system text, and the last user message; tools, then system, then messages is the invalidation order | automatic on OpenAI; passed through on OpenRouter |
| Thinking | provider default | omit `thinking`; depth through `output_config.effort` from the profile | none |
| Required fields | none | `max_tokens` | none |
| Auth and version | `Authorization: Bearer` | `x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | `Authorization: Bearer` |
| Idempotency | `Idempotency-Key` header | not documented; send nothing | not documented; send nothing |
| Errors | 401/403, 429, 5xx, timeout | the same plus 529 overloaded (retryable) and 413 | the same |

Error text today names OpenAI ("The OpenAI API key was rejected"). The display name moves into `ProviderProfile` so the wording is right for every provider without a per-provider branch.

### Provider profiles

A static table, one row per provider the setup page offers, plus a "custom" row the user fills in:

| id | family | endpoint | auth | default model |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| openai | responses | `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` | bearer | `gpt-5.4-mini` (today's) |
| openrouter | responses | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses` | bearer, plus `HTTP-Referer` and `X-Title` identifying JusPrin | to be chosen; the prompt evals use `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` |
| anthropic | anthropic | `https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages` | x-api-key | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| custom | responses or chat | user-entered base URL | bearer | user-entered |

The `JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` override becomes `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT`, applied to whichever profile is active, with the old name kept as an alias so the shell harness keeps working.

### Setup and configuration

- `SetupCredentials` gains nothing new for the named providers. The custom row adds `endpoint` (already a field) and `family`.
- `ProviderKeySetup` and `load_agent_runtime` call one factory, `make_provider_agent(profile, credentials, transport)`, instead of naming the class. The probe stays what it is: one real request with no project data.
- AppConfig keys stay as they are: `<provider>_api_key`, `provider`, `model`. A custom provider adds `endpoint` and `family` under the same section.
- The setup page flips Anthropic to available, replaces "Other…" with OpenRouter plus a custom entry, and keeps "which model to use is decided for you" for the named rows.

### Tests

The 33 adapter tests split by what they assert:

- **Loop tests** (about 20: call ordering, unrun answers, refusals, images after results, skills once, late completion, cancellation, usage) run against `ProviderAgent` with a scripted fake codec, so a provider bug cannot hide a loop regression and vice versa.
- **Wire tests** (about 13: body shape, replay of earlier calls, title request, attachment import availability, SSE parsing, error mapping) become one file per codec. The Responses file keeps today's assertions byte for byte.
- **Conformance test**: one scripted turn (text, two calls, one failed result, an image, a fired skill, text) is driven through every codec with canned provider streams, and the sequence of `AgentEvent`s must be identical. This is the test that keeps the loop neutral as codecs are added.
- **Golden bodies**: `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` is the oracle for the Responses codec. A refactor that changes a recorded body is a refactor that changed behaviour.
- **Live smoke**, opt-in with keys: one real request per provider, checked for a text reply and one tool call. Wire drift only shows up live, so this runs before a release, not in CI.

### Rollout

1. **Extract, no behaviour change.** Split `OpenAIResponsesAgent` into `ProviderAgent` + `ResponsesCodec` + `ProviderProfile`. Keep `OpenAIResponsesAgent` as a one-line alias so the harness and tests compile untouched. Prove the recorded request bodies are byte-identical before and after.
2. **OpenRouter.** Add the profile row, the setup page entry, the live smoke. Decide the default model.
3. **Anthropic.** Add `AnthropicCodec` with the schema projection, the wire tests, the conformance test, the setup entry, the live smoke. Add `cache_creation` to `AgentUsage` so cost reporting shows cache writes.
4. **Chat Completions**, only when a concrete host that lacks a Responses endpoint is wanted. Ollama and LM Studio are the likely reasons.

## MCP clients: what changes and what does not

The question was whether the design must account for how MCP clients (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code, through the stdio bridge) use the tools. Checked against `Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp`, `Mcp/McpCatalog.cpp` and the tool extension guide:

- **Nothing in the MCP server depends on the LLM adapter**, and the reverse is also true. Both project `ToolRegistry` definitions: the MCP side into `tools/list` with annotations from `ActionClass`, the LLM side into provider tool definitions. `ToolExecutionCoordinator` runs both. The provider split touches neither.
- **The registry schema dialect is the one shared contract.** It is consumed by the registry validator, by OpenAI strict mode, by Anthropic strict mode, and by whatever model sits behind an MCP client. The Anthropic finding above (five rejected keywords) is handled by projection inside the Anthropic codec, so the registry keeps its full schemas for MCP clients and for native validation. Rewriting the registry to Anthropic's subset would weaken what every MCP client is told and what the validator checks. Projection is also what Anthropic's own SDK helpers do.
- **Images beside results already have a neutral home.** `ToolActivity.image` is one record; MCP returns it as an image content block, Anthropic puts it in the `tool_result`, Responses sends it as a following user message. The codec table above is the only place that knows the difference.
- **The in-app agent should not reach its tools through MCP.** Both Anthropic's MCP connector and OpenAI's `mcp` tool type need a server reachable from the provider's side; the embedded server is loopback-only by design. Direct registry projection stays.
- **Tool names** are snake_case ASCII in the registry, which satisfies Anthropic's and OpenAI's name rules without renaming, so MCP clients and the in-app agent keep seeing the same names.

## Things to verify before building

My hypotheses, not confirmed facts:

- Anthropic's accepted character set for `tool_use` ids. An earlier turn answered by OpenAI (`call_…`) or OpenRouter would be replayed to Anthropic if the user switches provider mid-conversation. If Anthropic constrains the id format, the across-turn replay must mint its own ids for foreign calls.
- Whether Anthropic accepts two consecutive user messages. The host emits file-load reports as user-role entries that can sit next to the user's own message. If not, the codec merges adjacent same-role entries.
- Whether OpenRouter's Responses endpoint honours `instructions`, `strict`, `parallel_tool_calls` and image parts inside `function_call_output`. Its tool-calling page shows `strict: null` and does not document the first three. The prompt evals already send `instructions` successfully, which covers one of them.
- Whether to enable Anthropic's server-side refusal fallback (`fallbacks: "default"` with the `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` beta). It changes which model answers after a safety refusal, which is a product decision, so the design leaves it as a profile flag, off until decided.

## Sources

- [OpenRouter Responses API overview](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/responses/overview), [tool calling](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/responses/tool-calling), [reasoning](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/responses/reasoning)
- [Anthropic OpenAI SDK compatibility](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/libraries/openai-sdk)
- [Anthropic strict tool use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/strict-tool-use) and [structured outputs JSON Schema limitations](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs)
- [OpenAI reasoning guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning)

description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata:

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main
  checkout's build/arm64 cache has llvm-ar (commit 449b676145 documents it in
  agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md); any newly configured build dir
  gets Apple ar and fails again. Configure new dirs with the flags in
  [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
- Recurred 2026-09-14 on a fresh worktree at jusprin-newui bc19661a7f (archive
  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.
- A lasting fix (llvm-ar in the toolchain, thin archives, or less debug info)
  is Kenneth's call; the main checkout will hit this on its next growth.

Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

While working in a git worktree, a later `cmake --build build/arm64` and a
`git status` ran in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin` (the main checkout)
instead of the worktree, so one build reported "no work to do" and a status
check looked as if every edit had been lost.

with an absolute root are safest). Verify with `pwd` before trusting a
`git status` that looks wrong. See [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's

  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:


  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. A point's `once` (in `requests.json`) counts
  the last items of its request that the app sends on that request alone,
  a skill's text and, for the file-loaded skill, its picture; the runner
  drops them before it answers
  a read, as the app does.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the

  reaches the model, as that request's last item. The recorder checks that a
  point the script marks `"skill": "<name>"` ends with that skill (after the
  plate's picture for `file-loaded`), that no other point
  carries a skill or a picture, so an import's point carries the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
  first answered read) has none.
  A skill edit therefore needs a new recording, unlike a prompt edit.

What is written by hand is only what a model or a person would have said: the

## Judging a prompt or skill change

What the suite is for (Kenneth, 2026-10-19): showing that a change has not
made the prompt substantially worse. At three runs a case it detects large
regressions only, not small effects. Day-to-day host noise is small next to
what it looks for: on the printer suite the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74
of 84 on three runs.

1. After a prompt or skill change, run the "after" batch only: the checkout,
   same model, pinned hosts and judge, three runs a case. Compare it with the
   current baseline table below. There is no before run.
2. Judging the result. There are no fixed thresholds (Kenneth,
   2026-10-19). The agent running the batch compares it with the baseline
   case by case and reads every failure and unobserved run. It decides
   whether anything looks like a real regression worth investigating, and
   says why. A case with no baseline row is judged on its own expectation.
   When it is not sure, it asks Kenneth.
3. Only for a case that looks like a regression, run it again with
   `--prompt-rev <previous revision>` the same day. That tells the prompt
   apart from changed requests or a bad host day; a bad host day usually shows
   as drops in untouched cases too. A case run alone gets 20 runs, which is
   what to use before reading a smaller gap as real.
4. Baselines. The current baseline is one section. When Kenneth confirms a
   new result is good enough, it becomes the new baseline, and the old one
   moves to "Baseline history" below, kept for audit only and not used for
   comparison.

---README---
# Project chat prompt tests

The project chat's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`), the 28 project
tools and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` asks the live model for its next
step at a known point of a project chat and checks that step against one
sentence of the prompt. It is run against the prompt before an edit and after it, and the
counts compared. The app does not run.

On Kenneth's local machine, the keys are in
`~/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env` (outside the repository, mode `600`). An
agent running this suite can load them for that command in a subshell:

```bash
( . "$HOME/.config/jusprin/prompt-test.env"; tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py )
```

Do not print, copy into the repository, or include the key values in a command
or test log. The file exports `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_API_KEY`; the
runner reads them from its environment. No run happens without Kenneth
approving that batch (case count, runs, token estimate). A `403 Key limit
exceeded` means stop; do not switch keys.

The model, hosts and judge are the printer suite's (`tests/printer_prompt`,
"Which model"): DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, pinned to Alibaba,
Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud, with a pinned OpenAI judge.

## One step, with its reads answered

Each case starts at a point recorded from the app and judges the model's next
step: a reply, or its tool calls. One response may hold several calls. The
app asks for that (`parallel_tool_calls: true`) and runs every call in the
order the model wrote it, so every call is judged here:

- A change anywhere in the response (any call the registry does not mark
  read-only) is the step, whatever came before it; the first change if
  there are several. It ends the run, and nothing is answered.
- A response of reads only is checked read by read, in order, and the first
  read the case decides on is the outcome: `issue-fix` passes on a
  `settings_get` of its setting sent after a `workspace_inspect`.
- When the case decides on none of the reads (such as `workspace_inspect`
  before a reply), every one is answered with the result the app gave for
  that read at the same point, each under its own call id, and the model is
  asked again, at most three times (`MAX_READS`, counted in responses). As
  the app does, a read after one whose result did not succeed gets the
  app's "not run" result instead.
- If any read of the response has no recorded answer, none is answered and
  the run ends unobserved, so the history never holds a call without its
  result. A fourth response of reads ends it unobserved too.

A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either; it
is the step, reported beside it, and refusals are the C++ tests' business.
A run's report names every call of the response it ended on. `test_steps.py`
checks these rules offline against written model outputs, with no key and
nothing sent (`python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py`).

The recorded answers, kept beside each request, are the reads the script's
`answers` list names:

- `workspace_inspect` and `slice_report` with every section, given whatever
  sections the model asked for, and `printer_list`;
- `object_analyze` for every object on every plate with every `include`
  but `measure`, given for that object and session whatever it included;
  never with `measure` or `candidates`;
- `view_render` of every plate, and of the active plate with no plate named,
  in the `iso` and `plate` views, given for that plate and view whatever
  size the model asked for. Only the result's text is kept and replayed: the
  pinned hosts refuse any request that carries an image, so the picture the
  app sends after the result never reaches the model here;
- every setting, read with `settings_get`: of the print, of every object on
  every plate, of the selected filament and of the printer (355, 275 each,
  126 and 171 in the current recording). The keys come from the app itself:
  an empty `settings_search` query lists every setting of a scope, page by
  page. The filament's and printer's keys are also read under the print
  scope, and the print-wide settings under each object's scope, so a name
  asked for under the wrong scope gets the app's own answer, and so are three hand-kept lists of names the model takes from
  other slicers or invents (`fill_density`, `perimeters`,
  `initial_layer_height`...). A model's `settings_get` is answered with
  exactly the keys it asked for, in its order, each taken from those reads
  of the same scope and target, around the rest of the first such result;
- `settings_search` for 49 queries, given when the scope, target and
  words of the query match (case, spacing and word order aside), whatever
  `limit` or `writable` the model passed; never for `changedOnly`. A search
  result is the app's ranking for that query, so a wording not recorded has
  no answer.

They are real results the recorder got by calling those reads at that point
in the same turn; each case's point is replayed from the start for its own
recording, so those calls reach no other case's history. Recording all 22
points takes under three minutes. To keep `requests.json` small (about
3 MB), the recorder keeps each distinct setting item once, file-wide
(`settingItems`), and each point's workspace block once when a result
repeats it exactly (`sharedWorkspace`); the runner and the schema test put
both back byte for byte. A read outside these, or a `target` sent as a
string of JSON (which the app refuses), ends the run unobserved. Of the 38
distinct reads that ended runs unobserved in the runs of 2026-10-15, 26 are
now recorded; the other 12 are string targets, `changedOnly` searches,
search wordings not recorded, and setting names that do not exist in
OrcaSlicer.

This is not the design that failed on 2026-10-10. That one answered every
call, changes included, with stand-in results that did not hold what the
model asked for (`{"accepted": true}`), and let it run on: it wandered for 10
to 19 calls, provoked the behaviour it counted and spent over 300 million
tokens. Here only reads are answered, only with real results, and at most
three times. What this still gives up is whether the model chains changes on
its own across a conversation; only a run against the built app with real
results for every call can show that.

## What keeps it faithful to the app

- **The system prompt** comes from the page's own source, through
  `tests/printer_prompt/render_prompt.mjs` (`"kind": "project"`) and the page's
  esbuild. This needs node and the AgentUI npm install. `--prompt-rev REV`
  renders it as it was at a git revision, 6b4b8b6188 or later (the commit
  that moved the prompt from C++ to the page, unchanged).
- **`project_tools.json`** is the tool list the app sends in the project chat
  with nothing attached. `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` fails when it
  drifts from the registry. Regenerate it with
  `JUSPRIN_UPDATE_PROJECT_TOOLS=1 agent_bridge_tests '[project]'`.
- **Everything else in the request** is the app's: `requests.json`, recorded
  by the shell harness from `script.json`:

  ```bash
  build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness \
      --project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json tests/project_prompt/requests.json
  ```

  The harness runs the real app on its two-plate fixture (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
  0.4, Bambu PLA Basic, 0.20mm Standard, plate 1 sliced) with the project
  chat's real OpenAI adapter, but the adapter's requests go nowhere: each is
  answered with the next model output the script gives. The tools run for
  real, and the app builds every request itself: the earlier turns as
  `AgentHost::make_agent_request` replays them (calls with their results, a
  result over 16 KiB replaced by the omission note, at most 20 entries), the
  new message as `OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input` builds it (the
  person's words, then the app's `<print_issue>` and `<workspace>` blocks,
  each a part of its own), a canvas issue's message and context, a file-load report and its
  developer line, the file-loaded skill and the plate's picture on the
  request that first carries a load report, the print-issues skill on the
  request that carries a chip's message or first shows a slice's new
  warnings, the slice-failed skill on the request that first shows a
  refused or failed slice, the setup skill on the request that first
  carries a recorded or changed purpose or a setup change under one, and
  the live results of this turn's calls with the
  workspace block `AgentHost::continue_after_tool` adds. Arguments that need
  ids take them from the real previous result (`{{result/sessionId}}`) or the
  project (`{{workspace/activePlateId}}`). For each request it keeps, the
  harness checks the tools equal `project_tools.json` and the instructions
  equal `projectInstructions.fixture.txt`, then leaves both out of the file;
  the runner puts the rendered prompt and `project_tools.json` back. The
  script's `answers` list names the reads recorded at every point.
  `test_openai_responses_agent.cpp` also checks every recorded result and
  answer against its tool's output schema.
- **Answered reads** are added as the app continues a turn: the model's own
  output items, then a result for every call under its call id, in the order
  the calls were written. Each answer carries the action id and workspace
  block of the recorded call. A point's `once` (in `requests.json`) counts
  the last items of its request that the app sends on that request alone,
  a skill's text and, for the file-loaded skill, its picture; the runner
  drops them before it answers
  a read, as the app does.
- **Skills** (`AgentUI/src/skills/*/SKILL.md`) reach the model only in the
  recorded requests: the app adds one to the request where its event first
  reaches the model, as that request's last item. The recorder checks that a
  point the script marks `"skill": "<name>"` ends with that skill (after the
  plate's picture for `file-loaded`), that no other point
  carries a skill or a picture, so an import's point carries the
  file-loaded skill alone, and that the next request of the same turn (the
  first answered read) has none.
  A skill edit therefore needs a new recording, unlike a prompt edit.

What is written by hand is only what a model or a person would have said: the
person's words, the scripted calls, and two assistant replies (the summary
after the prepare turn and the first message about an opened file). The
scripted calls carry the replay form the app uses (`call_id`, `name`,
`arguments`); a live model's own item id, status and reasoning items within a
turn are not reproducible. Nothing checks that `requests.json` stays current:
record it again when a tool's results, the fixture or the request shape
change. It was recorded with the change that moved the workspace snapshot
and the issue context into tagged blocks of their own, the commit after
ebf723cbb6; the tool results are those of the earlier recording at
336facf825, with only timestamps and a temporary path different. Recorded

temporary path. Recorded again when the app began asking for several calls
per response (`parallel_tool_calls: true`): only that flag, ids, timestamps
and a temporary path changed.

The app streams its requests and this script does not.

## Cases

Each case names the sentence of `projectInstructions.ts` it tests (line
numbers at 6b4b8b6188) in its docstring, and observes one step. "A change" is
any tool the registry does not mark read-only: applying settings, slicing,

    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)

        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json

        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)

## Shape that landed (all under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent)

- `AgentTransport.hpp`: AgentHttpRequest (now a header list, with
  `header(name)` lookup), AgentHttpEvent, IAgentHttpTransport. Moved out of
  OpenAIResponsesAgent.hpp unchanged otherwise.
- `ProviderProfile.hpp`: ProviderProfile {id, family, endpoint, auth, model,
  display_name}; `openai_profile()` is the one row. The agent's config holds
  a *copy* of the row with the configured model/endpoint written over the
  defaults, so the codec reads `profile.model` and the loop reads
  `profile.endpoint`; no separate "model" field anywhere.
- `ProviderCodec.hpp`: AgentUsage (moved here), RequestKind, TurnTranscript
  (request_id + request_sequence, instructions, OfferedTool list, opening
  conversation as AgentConversationContext, user_content as neutral parts
  Text/Image/Pdf, steps[{assistant_turn (opaque json), results[{call_id,
  output_json, image}]}], once[] skills), ProviderToolCall, StreamEvent
  (TextDelta | TurnComplete{assistant_turn, calls, usage} | Incomplete |
  Failed{AgentError}), ProviderRequest {body, headers}, IProviderCodec
  {build, reset, parse}. Also `tagged_block()` (the `<workspace>` /
  `<print_issue>` wrapper) and `kConversationTitleInstructions`, shared by
  every codec.
- `ResponsesCodec.{hpp,cpp}`: the whole Responses wire format. Owns the
  strict rule (`has_closed_required_objects`), the Idempotency-Key header,
  the "The image returned by call X." user message, developer-role skill
  items, usage field names. `reset()` clears its per-response
  "completed seen" flag (the old class ignored a second response.completed).
- `ProviderAgent.{hpp,cpp}`: the loop, ported line for line. Owns
  workspace_json/drop_empty (the snapshot), attachment listing, base64 of
  attachment bytes, `available_in_app` + offered tool list with skill_read's
  description, yield filtering of skills, the refusal limit, http_error
  wording (with `profile.display_name`), SSE framing, generations.
- `OpenAIResponsesAgent.{hpp,cpp}`: now `struct OpenAIResponsesConfig`
  (unchanged fields, defaults taken from `openai_profile()`) and
  `class OpenAIResponsesAgent final : public ProviderAgent` with one
  converting constructor. AgentSetup.cpp, AgentConfiguration.cpp and
  shell_harness.cpp compile unchanged.

## Proof of no behaviour change

- `--project-prompt-requests tests/project_prompt/script.json <out>` run on
  the base commit and on the refactor, same build dir. Structural JSON diff
  of the 24 cases: 59 differing leaves, all of them timestamps (`updatedAt`,
  activity times), view_render PNG base64 + its `bytes` count, and temp
  paths. After normalising those four patterns: 0 differences. Script that
  did it: scratchpad of this session (not kept); it is ~30 lines of Python,
  easy to redo.
- agent_bridge_tests: 333 cases / 11649 assertions before, 340 / 11965
  after, all pass (`--order rand --rng-seed 0xBEEF`).
- Mutation check: reversing the queued call order (push_front) fails 3 loop
  tests and 1 wire test. (A first mutation, dropping `once.clear()` in
  post(), was a no-op because callers assign `once` before every post; the
  clear is the consumer-side statement of the rule, kept.)

## Things the next steps (OpenRouter, Anthropic) should know

- The loop checks "is this tool offered" by name against
  `m_transcript.tools`, not by re-running availability; a title request
  offers no tools, and `m_kind` still gates the refusal path exactly as
  `m_title_request` did.
- `StreamEvent::Incomplete` is worded by the loop ("stopped before
  finishing"); `Failed` carries the codec's full AgentError. HTTP status
  mapping stays in the loop; Anthropic's 529 should map to
  service_unavailable there (status >= 500 already does).
- A fake codec for loop tests lives in tests/agent/test_provider_agent.cpp

  touched here; re-record when the suite is next run.

  network, no GUI. The codec also keeps the old class's rule that a second
  response.completed in one stream is ignored.

Commit `8eb9ffada6` on branch `claude/provider-agent-extract` (worktree [.claude/worktrees/provider-agent-extract](.claude/worktrees/provider-agent-extract)) does rollout step 1: the OpenAI adapter is now a provider-neutral turn loop plus a Responses codec plus a provider profile, with no behaviour change. Not pushed, not merged.

**What changed**, all under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent`:

- **ProviderAgent** holds the turn loop, ported line for line. It owns a neutral transcript: instructions, offered tools, the earlier conversation, this turn's user content, one step per response with the provider's opaque assistant turn and its results, and the skills that ride on one request only.
- **IProviderCodec and ResponsesCodec** turn that transcript into a body and headers, and each streamed payload into neutral events. Pure, no network, no GUI. The strict rule, the idempotency header and the usage field names live only there.
- **ProviderProfile** is data: family, endpoint, auth style, default model, display name for error text. One row, `openai`.
- **AgentHttpRequest** carries a header list; the transport sends what it is given. `OpenAIResponsesAgent` is a thin subclass and `OpenAIResponsesConfig` keeps its fields, so setup, configuration and the harness compile unchanged.

**Tests**: the 33 adapter tests are split into 17 loop tests in [test_provider_agent.cpp](tests/agent/test_provider_agent.cpp), driven through a scripted fake codec, and 23 wire tests that keep their Responses assertions. A deliberately reversed call order fails three loop tests and one wire test. The full suite passes, 340 cases and 11965 assertions.

**Proof of no behaviour change**: the harness's request recorder was run on the base commit and on the refactor with the same build configuration. Across the 24 recorded request bodies and every tool answer, the only differences are timestamps, rendered PNG bytes and temp paths, which differ between any two runs. After normalising those, zero differences remain.

result.output:
**HTTP-Referer:** Required. The docs state: "This header is required for app attribution." If it's omitted, "no app page will be created and your usage will not appear in rankings."

**X-Title:** The docs don't label it required, and they describe only HTTP-Referer that way. X-Title is the older name for the display-name header, and it's still accepted: "`X-Title` is still supported for backwards compatibility."

**Newer header:** Yes, `X-OpenRouter-Title` is the current name for setting the app's display name. It doesn't create an app page on its own: "It must be paired with `HTTP-Referer`." The docs also say localhost apps must include `X-OpenRouter-Title` to be tracked.

input.command:
git status --short && git diff --stat && git add tests/agent/test_provider_live.cpp && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Meter the OpenRouter live smoke's spend, and record its first run

The live smoke in tests/agent/test_provider_live.cpp sends real, billed
requests to OpenRouter. It now logs every request on stderr as
"LIVE REQUEST n": the body size, model, tool count and
parallel_tool_calls sent, then the HTTP status, terminal event, response
id, tokens and cost. Cost is OpenRouter's usage.cost, which its docs say
every response carries (the old usage: {include: true} switch is
deprecated), or the listed price times the reported tokens when it is
absent. No request is sent unless the running total plus a bound on that
request's cost stays under $0.50. The bound counts two body bytes per
input token and allows 16k output tokens; the request itself sets no
output limit, so only a longer reply could pass the cap. The smoke also
honours JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT, so it can be dry-run against a local
stand-in for nothing. Two dry runs did that: one confirmed the metering
and the request flow, and one with an inflated reported cost confirmed
that the cap refuses a request.

First live run, 2026-10-19, approved by Kenneth with a $0.50 cap, model
openai/gpt-5.4-mini: all 3 cases and 22 assertions pass, in 4 requests
costing $0.0107 in total.

1. Instructions, strict and parallel calls: 34,881 bytes, 28 project
   tools, parallel_tool_calls true, strict on the closed tools.
   HTTP 200, 6,503 input and 7 output tokens, $0.0049. Reply
   "PINEAPPLE", as the instructions demanded. Instructions are honoured.
   strict and parallel_tool_calls are accepted, meaning not rejected;
   whether OpenRouter enforces or forwards them is not observable here,
   and its model listing does not name parallel_tool_calls.
2. Tool call: 34,956 bytes. HTTP 200, 6,514 input (6,400 cached) and
   20 output tokens, $0.0007. One workspace_inspect call, which passed
   the app's own validation. The tool prefix was served from the prompt
   cache.
3. Continuation after the result, with the image as a user message after
   it (the app's way): 35,565 bytes, 4 input items. HTTP 200, 6,593
   input (0 cached) and 17 output tokens, $0.0050. The reply was
   "Received the workspace inspect result, and no image came with it",
   so this run does not show that the model saw the image. The image was
   a 1x1 PNG and the question asked about the result, so the answer may
   be literal; a probe with a recognisable picture would settle it. The
   response held no reasoning item, so replaying reasoning on a
   continuation was not exercised.
4. Image inside a function_call_output (not what the app sends): 681
   bytes. HTTP 200, response.completed, 78 input and 5 output tokens,
   $0.00008. The shape is accepted. Whether the model saw the image is
   unknown: the log kept only the first 2,000 characters of the stream,
   and the reply fell after them.

Nothing in the provider profile needed to change. The Idempotency-Key
header the Responses codec sends was accepted.
EOF
git log --oneline -4
